Between the model and the customer sits a great deal of unglamorous, domain-specific work: orchestrating context across dozens of connected systems, encoding the logic of how sales and marketing teams actually operate, handling permissions and compliance, and integrating with the messy reality of Fortune 500 IT environments. This work is the new GTM application layer—and that is where new GTM companies are building. This shift does not mean the end of the CRM. Salesforce still owns its database; HubSpot still owns its database; customer data continues to live where it has always lived, for the reasons it has always lived there. Just as the Feed expanded social media's TAM to "everything you're interested in," the Agent revolution is expanding what software can reasonably charge for, without destroying the human budgets that fund most current GTM efforts. A new generation of companies is building on this emerging layer. The next generation of GTM software will be written there.

Institutional memory becomes something a company can truly "ship." Additionally, the VP of Sales can now genuinely know what her team is doing.
